item.title: Americans don’t have to choose between our AI future and ripping off copyright owners
item.description: The DOJ's embrace of fair use for AI training breaks with the White House's own framework, as OpenAI, Microsoft and news groups battle over copyright.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest court battles over artificial intelligence (AI) is putting an age-old legal principle to the test — and raising important questions about the Trump administration's AI policy.

Several news organizations, including The New York Times, are suing OpenAI and Microsoft for using millions of newspaper articles to train AI systems. The newspapers argue that the tech firms violated basic copyright protections. The tech firms contend that training their models on those articles qualifies as "fair use," a longstanding principle that allows copyrighted material to be used in certain ways without permission from or compensation to the copyright owner.

The Department of Justice (DOJ) has sided squarely with OpenAI's position — breaking with the administration's previously more balanced stance on the issue. The DOJ filed a statement of interest embracing an extreme vision of fair use that would grant AI companies virtually unfettered access to copyrighted material for commercial training, without obtaining permission from or compensating the creators whose works fuel these systems.

MIKE DAVIS: THE TRUMP DOJ SHOULD WITHDRAW ITS STATEMENT OF INTEREST IN THE OPENAI LAWSUIT

This expansive interpretation threatens to turn a narrow copyright exception into a blanket exemption for the world's most powerful and profitable industries.

The DOJ's reasoning is that requiring a copyright license for material used in AI training would impose high costs on AI developers. It claims those costs could make it harder for small companies to compete and hamper U.S. AI leadership and national security.

FOX NEWS POLL: VOTERS SEE AI REGULATION AS URGENT, RANK SAFEGUARDS AHEAD OF INNOVATION

Those concerns deserve consideration. But the DOJ's aggressive arguments in the brief depart from more measured guidance elsewhere in the administration. The White House's official AI framework acknowledges valid arguments on both sides of the copyright debate.

Likewise, the Carolina Principles for Emerging Technologies, adopted by G20 ministers at the Commerce Department's recent Innovation Ministerial, recognize that the intersection of AI and copyright poses "complex legal and policy questions." The principles note the "essential role" of copyright protections in supporting creators and call for respecting IP as a pillar of G20 AI policy.

MUSIC INDUSTRY FENDS OFF FLOOD OF AI MUSIC 'STEALING' THE CHARTS

The DOJ statement also overlooks how its stance could favor larger AI companies over smaller firms and startups. Several AI startups have argued that paying for the material they use provides more reliable access to training material, reduces legal uncertainty and improves models. Other companies have emerged to aggregate copyrights and make licensing easier.

It's particularly problematic for large AI companies to complain about paying for access to copyrighted materials. They are among the best positioned to pay for those materials, and doing so would help develop the kind of licensing markets they claim are lacking.

OBAMA CRITICIZES TRUMP ON APPROACH TO AI, ESCALATES WARNING FOR STRONGER REGULATION

And even if national security were a legitimate justification, the government could not simply disregard property rights. The Constitution and other laws require just compensation when private property is taken for public use, and intellectual property rights are still property rights. Letting AI firms appropriate creators' IP without permission or compensation would be akin to letting data center builders seize private land without paying fair value.

If courts adopt the DOJ's position that fair use protects AI developers in virtually all circumstances, it would reduce incentives to create new works. Copyrights encourage creative work by assuring writers, artists and other creators that their work can't be easily stolen or copied. Licensing those rights allows creators to earn a living and underpins over $1 trillion in U.S. economic activity.

Weaker copyrights could result in fewer human-created books, articles, research papers, films and songs. Ironically, that could eventually leave AI systems with fewer and lower-quality materials to train on – a scenario that serves no one's interests.

All of this is why the Trump administration would be wise to follow its own AI framework and let the court system evaluate AI copyright disputes case by case, rather than arguing for unfettered fair use exceptions.

Policymakers also have a role to play. One promising bill is the bipartisan CLEAR Act. Introduced in February by California Democrat Sen. Adam Schiff and Utah Republican Sen. John Curtis, the CLEAR Act would require AI developers to publicly disclose the copyrighted works used in each new generative-AI model's training dataset.

The proposal would not settle whether any particular training practice qualifies as fair use. But it would give creators more information about whether their work helped train an AI system, enabling them to pursue appropriate compensation or other remedies when they believe their rights have been violated.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That kind of targeted reform offers a useful model for copyright enforcement in the age of AI. Rather than treating licensing as an obstacle to innovation, policymakers should foster a market where AI developers can efficiently license copyrighted material while respecting creators' rights.

AI innovation is vital to America's future. But America's creative industries still depend on strong copyright protections. Policymakers need to promote both.

item.title: New York Dem addresses bizarre 'lizard people' claims after viral clip behind Mamdani
item.description: New York Assemblyman Jordan J.G. Wright breaks silence on viral reptilian claims after a clip showed him rolling his eyes behind Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
item.content:encoded:
A Democratic New York City assemblyman addressed bizarre "lizard people" conspiracy theories after a viral video appeared to show his eyes rolling backward while standing behind Mayor Zohran Mamdani during a press conference.

Jordan J.G. Wright was spotted during a press conference behind Mamdani on Friday, when the city announced plans to eventually shut down Rikers Island.

As Mamdani spoke, Wright appeared to flash a slight grin before blinking and rolling his eyes in a circular motion toward the back of his head, prompting a wave of bizarre speculation online.

"I have no idea what was going on in that video. I’m really not sure," Wright told the New York Post in a statement.

NYC MAYOR MAMDANI ANNOUNCES DELAYED PLAN TO CLOSE CITY'S LARGEST JAIL

He added that his work as an assemblyman speaks to his human character, pointing to a project he championed in Harlem that serves as the city's first community-based center dedicated to climate action. The five-story hub provides residents with environmental education and advocacy.

"Obviously I’m a human being, and my humanity can be seen through my legislation like the $4 million for the WE ACT environmental justice center in Harlem," he said. "I can’t speak to any reptiles or aliens."

The video sent social media users into a frenzy over the weekend, reigniting a decades-old conspiracy theory that extraterrestrial reptilians secretly control the Earth by disguising themselves as world leaders and celebrities to manipulate society.

"This is how lizards blink… I am pretty sure there is full-blown ‘Men in Black’ aliens walking among us disguised as human beings, and they are hiding in plain sight," one social media user said, according to the Post.

NYC SUSPECT IN CHINATOWN FATAL BEATING HAD 5 OPEN CASES AS MAMDANI PUSHES PLAN TO CLOSE RIKERS

Another X user suggested the clip showed that aliens were becoming increasingly brazen about revealing themselves to the public.

"The ‘reptile’ is standing right behind Mamdani, as he announces a full scale-release of dangerous prisoners from NYC jails," the X user said.

"The aliens are not even bothering to hide themselves anymore. They intend to create so much chaos on Earth, that we will be unable to defend ourselves," the user added.

The discussion also spilled onto Reddit, where some users questioned whether Wright was human.

"Yes, the guy in the back is a reptilian, 100%" the Reddit user said.

MAMDANI IGNITES ONLINE FIRESTORM AFTER MOURNING DEATH OF INMATE CHARGED IN GRISLY MURDER: 'WTF ARE WE DOING?'

Wright, the son of former Assemblyman Keith L.T. Wright and grandson of former New York Supreme Court Judge Bruce Wright, represents New York's 70th Assembly District in Harlem.

He was reelected without opposition in November after defeating Democratic socialist Conrad Blackburn in the Democratic primary in June. His legislative priorities include affordable housing, health care access and public safety, according to his profile.

A lifelong New Yorker and Central Harlem resident, Wright graduated from Syracuse University in 2017 with a degree in psychology.

Wright stood behind Mamdani on Friday as the mayor announced plans to cut New York City's jail population by 2,500 inmates over the next five years and close the city’s largest jail by 2032.

The remaining inmates, estimated at 4,100 detainees, will be moved to four new, smaller borough-based jails opening in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx.

Fox News Digital reached out to Jordan J.G. Wright for comment.

item.title: Cam Skattebo ignores his own backflip celebration retirement promise at end of Giants victory Jaguars
item.description: Cam Skattebo vowed to retire his backflip celebration, then did one anyway after the New York Giants clinched their 23-18 win over Jacksonville.
item.content:encoded:
There are some things about Cam Skattebo that the New York Giants can definitely count on: he is going to bring energy, he's still in danger of fumbling and he should not be trusted when he says he's going to put the backflip on the back burner.

Two of those three are not optimal.

One of those three is really moronic.

LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY

CAM SKATTEBO PUTTING HIS BACKFLIP ON THE BACK BURNER AFTER SEEING AIDAN HUTCHINSON CELEBRATION INJURY

Days after telling reporters he was going to retire from his signature backflip celebration, Skattebo apparently decided to ignore everything he said (good advice for all of us, actually) and performed one of his semi-plyometric flights near the end of the Giants game on Sunday.

"When energy calls for it, it calls for it," Skattebo boldly explained to reporters after the game. "My teammates, I do whatever I can to bring the energy for the team and play this game with my heart and soul. So when that happens, it's second nature.

"It's hard to hold back."

You want to know the dumb part about this explanation? Neither energy, nor the team were calling for Skattebo to perform a backflip at the moment he did.

The Giants had clinched their 23-18 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars with two minutes to play when Skattebo delivered a 5-yard run. The game was effectively over.

But that's when Skattebo forgot everything he said about not risking an injury the way he watched Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson did on Nov. 15 – which was by leaving his feet to perform a celebration.

DAN CAMPBELL WON'T STOP PLAYERS FROM CELEBRATING EVEN AFTER STAR AIDAN HUTCHINSON WAS INJURED CELEBRATING

Hutchinson, by the way, last week promised he's done going airborne.

So, Skattebo did his unretired backflip when the game was decided. And wouldn't it have been utterly embarrassing if he'd done that backflip upon clinching a victory, injured himself needlessly, and been unable to play in the coming weeks?

Skattebo had coach John Harbaugh previously convinced he had gained some wisdom after the coach read the player's quotes about his backflip last Friday.

Harbaugh actually said in a press conference he was thinking of discussing the matter with Skattebo, but decided it wasn't necessary because the running back seemed to understand the celebration might not be in his or the team's best interest.

But, nope.

Skattebo in the air, feet above his head, relying on his feet and ankles to hold up during the landing and hoping his knees don't buckle.

So, a conversation with Harbaugh is likely incoming.

Skattebo is obviously valuable to the Giants. It's the reason they're not thrilled with these backflips in the first place.

But while he's important to the team, he's also kind of just a solid player. If he weren't playing in New York, the chances of him being a marketing thing would be far smaller because, well, take Sunday as an example:

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He rushed 14 times for 34 yards — a 2.4-yard-per-carry average.

He caught three passes for 14 yards.

And fumbled once, which he lost.

So the guy is solid. And hard to figure out. And something of a frustration for Harbaugh.

item.title: 49ers' George Kittle channels his inner Luchador as he sports WWE star's mask, performs celebration after TD
item.description: San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle channeled WWE's Penta with the "Cero Miedo" celebration after a touchdown against the Vikings in Mexico City.
item.content:encoded:
The Lucha Libre spirit was strong with San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle on Sunday.

Kittle channeled WWE star Penta as he walked into Estadio Banorte in Mexico City before his game against the Minnesota Vikings, and a few moments later, he celebrated a touchdown in a similar fashion.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

The tight end caught a touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to give the 49ers an early lead in the first quarter. He quickly emulated his favorite WWE wrestler, hitting the "Cero Miedo" – or "Zero Fear" – celebration. His teammates joined in as well.

Kittle is a noted WWE superfan. He appeared at WrestleMania 39 in Inglewood, California, at SoFi Stadium and got involved in an impromptu match. He hit The Miz with a clothesline. It allowed Pat McAfee to score the win over The Miz. The two then posed in the ring.

He appeared on the "Bussin’ with the Boys" podcast last year and explained that he woud like to be involved in WWE at some point when his career in the NFL is finished.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"I would love to do WWE," he said. "I think there's definitely an opportunity within that world, and I would love nothing more than to be a part of it."

But don’t expect Kittle to retire any time soon.

When he’s healthy, Kittle is still putting up video-game numbers on the field. The seven-time Pro Bowler appears to be back at full strength after a season-ending injury last year. He came into the game against the Vikings with 44 catches for 557 yards and five touchdown catches.

You can add another hot start on the board for him and San Fran.

item.title: Purdue professor, 2 daughters killed in apparent murder-suicide after daughter’s terrifying 911 call
item.description: Purdue University professor Julie Tkach and her two teenage daughters died in an apparent murder-suicide in West Lafayette, Indiana, authorities say.
item.content:encoded:
This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or 1-800-273-TALK (8255).

A Purdue University professor and her two teenage daughters were killed in an apparent murder-suicide last week after the father reportedly opened fire on his family before turning the gun on himself, according to Indiana authorities.

Preliminary autopsy results identified the mother as Julie Tkach, 53, of West Lafayette, who died from multiple gunshot wounds, with her death ruled a homicide, the Tippecanoe County Coroner’s Office said Friday. Julie was a clinical assistant professor in Purdue University's Department of Hospitality and Tourism Management, according to her LinkedIn profile.

The father, Thomas Tkach, 51, died by suicide from a gunshot wound to the head, officials said. He was employed by the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office as a courthouse security officer after previously serving as a jail deputy, according to local outlet Star City News., according to local outlet Star City News.

KANSAS CONVICTED FELON, SEX OFFENDER ALLEGEDLY KILLS FELLOW FAMILY MEMBERS BEFORE TAKING HIS OWN LIFE: POLICE

Their daughter, Katharyn, 17, died from multiple gunshot wounds to the head, while their other daughter, Lauren, 16, died from multiple gunshot wounds, the coroner's office said.

West Lafayette Police said the family members were found inside their West Lafayette-area home Wednesday evening, Nov. 18, after officers responded to a 911 call shortly after 8:30 p.m. The coroner's office was subsequently notified of multiple deaths at roughly 1:50 a.m. Thursday.

According to emergency dispatch audio obtained by Star City News, authorities received a separate concerning call shortly before the bodies were discovered. A dispatcher described receiving a call from one of the daughters.

"She advised that her father had a gun and was threatening to shoot the family. I heard multiple gunshots go off and the line is now silent," the recording said.

TWO TEEN SUSPECTS HELD AFTER 5 FAMILY MEMBERS KILLED IN 'TARGETED MASS SHOOTING'

While officials have not disclosed a motive behind the killings, the coroner’s office urged anyone struggling with mental health challenges to seek help through available resources. Residents can call or text 988 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

Indiana State Police is leading the investigation because Thomas Tkach was employed by the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office.

The West Lafayette Police Department described the incident as a "terrible night" that deeply affected its personnel, as well as those at the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office, which also responded to the scene.

"Many people on my team and other teams have had a very difficult time with the incident that took place on Wednesday night," the sheriff’s office said.

"The things seen and heard the other night will be remembered for the rest of their lives," the office added.

DISPATCH AUDIO RELEASED IN MICHIGAN FAMILY MURDER-SUICIDE AS TROUBLED FAMILY'S SECRETS EMERGE

According to LinkedIn, Julie had spent more than 20 years teaching and mentoring students in the hospitality industry. Prior to Purdue, she worked at South Dakota State University for eight years as a lecturer and instructor.

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Purdue offered its condolences and said it would provide support to those affected.

"We are saddened by this tragedy and the death of Julie and her family. We offer our condolences and support to her colleagues, peers, students and all who are affected," the university said. 

"The Tippecanoe County Coroner’s Office extends its deepest condolences to all who have been impacted by this tragedy. These deaths have affected many people across our community, including friends, neighbors, and others who knew the family," the office said.

The emergency response required a multi-agency effort involving the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office, West Lafayette Police Department, Indiana State Police, emergency medical services, fire crews and the coroner's office, according to West Lafayette police.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Tippecanoe County Sheriff's Office and Purdue University for more information.

item.title: Russian warship sinks off Libya as suspected Ukrainian strikes take war beyond Black Sea
item.description: The Russian corvette Merkury capsized at Benghazi Naval Base after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck, injuring ten people, Libyan officials say.
item.content:encoded:
A Russian warship capsized and sank Sunday after suspected Ukrainian sea drones struck a naval base in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire, according to Libyan officials.

Hours later, a second drone attack also hit a commercial ship off the coast of Benghazi, Reuters reported.

The first ship, the Russian navy corvette Merkury, was docked at Benghazi Naval Base when two explosive-laden sea drones struck the vessel, according to Libyan military officials who spoke to The Associated Press.

UKRAINE POUNDS BLACK SEA FLEET’S ‘LAST MAJOR STRONGHOLD’ WHILE PUTIN FLEXES NAVAL POWER IN PACIFIC

At least four other drones were intercepted and destroyed, the officials said.

Satellite images showed most of the warship capsized and submerged, with only its bow remaining above water. Smoke could be seen rising from the ship's superstructure, and debris was scattered along the pier.

Ten people, including Russian and Libyan nationals, suffered minor injuries in the attack and were receiving treatment in Benghazi, medical sources told Reuters.

The warship had stopped at the port to refuel and resupply while returning to Russia under a maritime cooperation agreement with Libya's eastern-based government, officials said in a statement.

Libyan military officials said an initial investigation indicated that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched from a base in western Libya, according to The AP.

UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA’S ARCTIC GAS HEARTLAND AS TRUMP PUSHES PUTIN TOWARD PEACE

Hours after the warship was struck, a Maltese-flagged commercial ship was also hit by a sea drone off Benghazi, two Libyan military sources told Reuters.

Libyan naval forces rescued the commercial ship's crew, while health officials reported that some crew members sustained minor injuries and were in stable condition.

Libyan naval and air forces also intercepted more than 20 drone boats off Benghazi on Sunday evening, the military sources told Reuters.

The attacks prompted Libya's eastern-based government to seek an international investigation.

Prime Minister Osama Hamad said his government had submitted a formal request to the United Nations General Assembly and Security Council to investigate the attacks, including suspicions that the drones were launched from western Libya.

RUSSIA DEPLOYS NORTH KOREAN MISSILE UNIT TO UKRAINE; MOSCOW-PYONGYANG AXIS DEEPENS: REPORT

Hamad also called for an investigation into the possible presence of Ukrainian military experts in Libya and requested an explanation from Kyiv about their activities.

The eastern government insisted that Libya was not a party to the war between Russia and Ukraine and condemned attempts to use its territory to settle foreign conflicts.

"The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts," the government said.

Benghazi is controlled by forces loyal to Gen. Khalifa Haftar, whose self-styled Libyan National Army dominates eastern and southern Libya and maintains close ties with Russia.

Libya has been divided since the 2011 NATO-backed uprising that toppled longtime dictator Moammar Gadhafi.

UKRAINE UNLEASHES MORE THAN 400 DRONES NEAR MOSCOW IN ONE OF WAR'S BIGGEST ATTACKS

A U. N. recognized government operates from Tripoli, while a rival administration controls much of the east.

The suspected attacks also come as Ukraine has expanded its campaign against Russian naval assets beyond the Black Sea. In December 2025, Ukraine said it struck a Russian-linked oil tanker with aerial drones in the Mediterranean Sea.

In March 2026, Russia accused Ukraine of attacking a Russian liquefied natural gas tanker with naval drones launched from the Libyan coast.

Libyan officials previously told the AP that Ukrainian drone specialists had been operating from military facilities in western Libya, including an air base in Misrata and sites in Tripoli and Zawiya.

Since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Ukrainian forces have used explosive-laden sea drones and missiles to strike Russian warships and naval installations, primarily in the Black Sea.

item.title: Mark Ruffalo doubles down on call to oust Schumer over 'entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties'
item.description: Actor Mark Ruffalo said Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., is too beholden to "entrenched religious beliefs" to lead, sparking bipartisan backlash from critics.
item.content:encoded:
Actor Mark Ruffalo said Sen. Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., was too beholden to "entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties" to lead the Senate in a post on X, advocating for Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., as Senate majority leader.

"Israel is just one issue in a whole host of reasons Van Hollen is the right leader for our times. We need Justice, we need leadership that follows the will of the people not entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties," Ruffalo wrote on X. "Does not follow entrenched fossil fuel and corporate interests, nor throws a blind eye to the hard realties [sic] we face today."

The four-time Academy Award nominee argued that Van Hollen had the integrity, strength and spirit to fight "the social and moral corruption that has set in with age-old presumptions" in the incoming Democratic-led Congress.

BILL MAHER BLASTS DEMOCRATIC PARTY, SAYS IT IS FINE WITH RELIGION 'AS LONG AS THAT FAITH ISN’T JEWISH'

"We have absolutely nothing to lose by replacing Sen. Schumer," Ruffalo wrote. "We can only gain more justice and freedom. Put pressure on your senators. Now is the time. Keep the momentum of this election going. Thank you, Senator Schumer, but it’s time to move aside."

Ruffalo faced backlash across both sides of the political aisle for what critics viewed as a slight against Schumer's Jewish background.

"Entrenched religious beliefs? Entrenched loyalties? Please elaborate, @MarkRuffalo," Anti-Defamation League CEO and National Director Jonathan Greenblatt wrote. "Which religion? Loyal to whom?"

"There are many devout Senators & Congressmen with 'entrenched religious beliefs.' Chuck Schumer is not one of them," Rabbi Yaakov Menken, executive vice president of the Coalition for Jewish Values, wrote. "Van Hollen is far more tied to the Episcopal Bishop of Washington than Schumer is to any leading Rabbi. Guess what really bothers Ruffalo."

RABBINIC GROUP ACCUSES JEWISH ENTERTAINERS OF 'WHITEWASHING ANTISEMITISM' IN MARK RUFFALO DEFENSE

"Can you clarify what you mean by 'entrenched religious beliefs and loyalties'?" political commentator Meghan McCain asked.

By Sunday, Ruffalo doubled down on his post, citing Schumer's 2018 comments at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) annual policy conference where he was quoted saying, "Of course, we say it’s our land, the Torah says it, but they don’t believe in the Torah. So that’s the reason there is not peace."

"These are Senator Schumer’s words, not mine," Ruffalo added on X.

"Schumer is entitled to his religious beliefs, but those beliefs cannot determine the rights of another people. And they certainly cannot substitute for international law," Ruffalo continued. "This is a conflict about land, freedom, security, equality and self-determination. Peace requires justice, accountability and respect for the rights of both Palestinians and Israelis."

Fox News Digital reached out to Ruffalo's representative and Schumer's office for comment.

MORE THAN 180 JEWISH ENTERTAINERS RALLY BEHIND ACTOR MARK RUFFALO IN PROTEST LETTER

Human rights attorney Brooke Goldstein, executive director of The Lawfare Project and Founder of the #EndJewHatred movement, denounced Ruffalo's posts, calling the actor "obsessively fixated" on the Jewish state to the point of questioning members of the party he supports.

"And now they’re even turning on one of their own, Senator Chuck Schumer, because apparently even being a loyal Democrat isn’t enough when you’re Jewish," Goldstein told Fox News Digital. "They’re saying the quiet part out loud now, no longer afraid to invoke his Jewish identity as grounds for distrust. The message is unmistakable: ‘He’s a Jew. We can’t trust him.'"

"His [Ruffalo's] obsessive fixation on the Jewish state, his selective outrage, and his breathtaking moral relativism raise serious questions about whether his "so called activism" is driven by genuine concern for America’s interests or by hostility toward Jews," she added.

Ruffalo previously faced accusations of antisemitism after he criticized the Paramount merger earlier this year, focusing on CEO David Ellison and his father's history of supporting Israel.

item.title: Urgent warning issued to cruise passengers about strict new law in Mexico
item.description: Cruise passengers visiting Mexico with minors need passports, birth certificates and notarized letters under a new law. The government passed the measure to combat child trafficking.
item.content:encoded:
Cruise passengers are being warned they may need to provide extensive documentation for onshore activities at ports in Mexico.

The sweeping law now requires adults traveling to Mexico with minors to prove their relationship to the children in the group, or face denial of service at hotels, resorts and tours, the "Royal Caribbean Blog" reported.

Effective Nov. 14, 2026, an amendment to Mexico's General Tourism Law places pressure on tourism providers to verify family relationships, according to Travel Market Report.

CRUISE TIPPING CHARGES ARE 'OUT OF CONTROL' SAY PASSENGERS AS COMPANIES TOUT 'EXCEPTIONAL SERVICE'

The Mexican Senate unanimously passed the measure to combat child trafficking and exploitation, aiming to shed the country's status as a major destination for such crimes.

"Pedophiles don't come to Mexico by chance," noted Sen. Laura Esquivel Torres, as reported by the same blog. 

"Starting today, we will begin to shut down these opportunities," Torres added. 

Fox News Digital reached out to Sen. Torres and Royal Caribbean for additional information.

POPULAR CRUISE LINE'S BIKINI CRACKDOWN COULD SURPRISE PASSENGERS AT ISLAND PORTS

Tourism operators are legally required to check documents and must notify authorities if an adult cannot prove legal guardianship or parentage, according to news outlet TravelHost.

Travelers should be prepared to present passports, long-form birth certificates and custody or guardianship paperwork, the same blog noted. 

Documentation explaining any differing last names between a parent and child is also recommended.

Even if cruise passengers are only stopping in a Mexican port for the day, the rules apply to all local services.

11-NIGHT CARIBBEAN CRUISE ABRUPTLY CANCELED AFTER COAST GUARD DETAINS SHIP

While simply disembarking from a cruise ship might not trigger a document check, booking a beach club day pass, a local snorkeling excursion or renting a vacation home likely will, the blog reported (it is not affiliated with Royal Caribbean).

Travelers are urged to call hotels and tour operators in advance to confirm paperwork requirements.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The Mexican government has not yet released an official checklist, but travel experts advise bringing a folder with these documents, according to the same blog:

Travelers have been taking to Reddit to weigh in on the new rules.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"This is going to be a mess," one person wrote. 

"There has been no formal guidance given by the Mexican government on what will be accepted and different hotels (including different people at the same hotel) have been giving different answers," the same commenter added.

"Bring all government docs and letters from parent authorizing you to have [temporary] guardianship of their kids for travel," another Reddit user said. "Not that hard, really."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I own a travel agency and [before that] was a Spanish teacher for 17 years. [I] traveled to Mexico with my students every summer and I always had a form for this — they used to often check," a third Reddit user said.

Another chimed in, "My only issue with using the birth [certificate] proof is that a passport and birth certificate are often the only, or certainly the two most important identity documents, a child has. Having both lost or stolen while out of the country would be very stressful to deal with."

"I also don’t understand why it matters for hotels," the Reddit user added.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Mexican Embassy in the United States, Mexico's Secretariat of Tourism and World Vision Mexico for more information.

item.title: 'Yes, Dear' star Anthony Clark's cause of death revealed: report
item.description: Anthony Clark's cause of death was septic shock, with influenza A and chronic alcoholism as underlying conditions and acute kidney failure a factor.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Clark's official cause of death was due to septic shock, according to a death certificate obtained by People magazine. He was 62.

The "Yes, Dear" star died on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Influenza A and chronic alcoholism were included as underlying conditions, the outlet reported.

In addition, acute kidney failure was listed as a significant contributing factor in Clark's death.

'YES, DEAR' STAR ANTHONY CLARK DEAD AT 62

"Anthony was one of the funniest and most talented comedians and actors I have ever had the pleasure of watching," his longtime manager, Barry Katz, told Fox News Digital.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"It was an honor to represent him and he will be missed for the joy, happiness, and love he brought to everyone he worked with and the audiences that were blessed to see his undeniable performances."

Clark's "Yes, Dear" co-star, Mike O'Malley, initially shared the news of his death in a tribute posted on X. Deadline then reported that Clark died of "complications related to pneumonia and the flu."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

"Anthony Clark died yesterday. He was a hilarious guy," O'Malley wrote. "When my wife Lisa and I were dating back in the mid-nineties, Anthony was already famous in Boston, regularly selling out comedy shows. The first time we saw him at The Comedy Connection, we laughed and laughed and laughed.

STACY KEACH DEAD AT 85 AS ‘MIKE HAMMER’ STAR’S WIFE SHARES EMOTIONAL TRIBUTE

"He was so unique — one of those comics who is laughing along with you at the absurdity of his stories and observations. I was a fan before I was a friend. We spoke on the phone three weeks ago. He had us laughing loudly once again. Attached are some snapshots from our last episode of Yes Dear, which ended 20 years ago after 122 episodes. Rest in peace. Tony."

Born in 1964, the Virginia native kickstarted his career in comedy at an early age. In 1986, Clark, who graduated from Emerson College with a mass communication degree, won a national college comedy award.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Clark starred in NBC’s "Boston Common" from 1996 to 1997, followed by "Soul Man" opposite Dan Aykroyd. His biggest success, however, came with "Yes, Dear," which ran from 2000 to 2006 alongside O’Malley, Jean Louisa Kelly and Liza Snyder.

His film credits include "Dogfight," "The Thing Called Love" and "The Rock." He also appeared on "Ellen" and hosted the fourth season of "Last Comic Standing" in 2006.

item.title: Chiefs and Bills take care of business ahead of the NFL’s biggest regular-season game
item.description: The Kansas City Chiefs beat Arizona 34-7 and the Buffalo Bills handled Miami 26-9 to set up a Thanksgiving showdown in the race for the AFC’s No. 1 seed.
item.content:encoded:
Sunday in the NFL felt a little like November in the SEC for the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills. You know how SEC teams like to schedule a late-season cupcake as a tune-up before the big rivalry game? Well, the Chiefs and Bills don’t get to pick their opponents, but whoever put together the Week 11 schedule did them both a favor.

When I wrote about the Week 11 betting lines Thursday, Buffalo was favored by 16.5 points and Kansas City by 15.5. Both covered those numbers. The Bills beat the Miami Dolphins, 26-9, while the Chiefs demolished the Arizona Cardinals, 34-7.

Of course, the analogy only works if the cupcake leads into a big rivalry game. And that’s exactly what’s in store for NFL fans on Thanksgiving night, when Patrick Mahomes and the 8-2 Chiefs head to Buffalo to face Josh Allen and the 9-1 Bills. The Bills have never hosted a game on Thanksgiving, and for their first one, they get the biggest game of the NFL regular season.

Sure, Chiefs-Bills doesn’t have the history of Steelers-Browns, Cowboys-Eagles or Packers-Lions. But try telling someone in Buffalo that Kansas City isn’t a rival. Mahomes and Allen met in the playoffs four times in five seasons, twice with a trip to the Super Bowl on the line. The Chiefs ended the Bills’ season all four times. And I’m guessing nobody in Buffalo needs me to explain what "13 seconds" means.

DK METCALF DISQUALIFIED FROM STEELERS GAME FOR UNSPORTSMANLIKE PENALTIES INCLUDING POKING OPPONENT'S FACEMASK

Kansas City certainly looked ready Sunday. Travis Kelce had a vintage Kelce game, catching six passes for 74 yards and two touchdowns, both before halftime. Mahomes threw for 324 yards and three scores, and rookie running back Emmett Johnson added 105 yards and a touchdown on the ground. That’s three straight games with at least 34 points for the Chiefs.

Buffalo, meanwhile, won by 17 on a day when Allen threw two interceptions and didn’t run the ball once. How often do you get to say that about a Bills win? Allen still threw for 304 yards, and Miami managed three field goals. I wouldn’t count on Mahomes being quite that accommodating.

The Bills have won five straight regular-season games against the Chiefs. A sixth would put Buffalo at 10-1, two games ahead of Kansas City. If the Chiefs win, they’ll close out Thanksgiving night tied with Buffalo at 9-2 and holding the head-to-head tiebreaker. That’s a pretty big swing for a Bills team trying to earn the AFC’s No. 1 seed for the first time in the Josh Allen era.

Allen has won all three of his regular-season trips to Arrowhead and lost all three of his playoff games there. Mahomes has won in Buffalo in January, too, beating the Bills 27-24 in the divisional round after the 2023 season. But both times these two played for the AFC championship, Buffalo had to go to Kansas City. A win Thursday gives Allen a much better shot at making Mahomes get on a plane in late January.

And if you’re wondering what happened the last time Buffalo did earn the No. 1 seed, the 1993 Bills won the AFC championship game at home, 30-13. The team they beat to get to the Super Bowl? The Kansas City Chiefs.

BUFFALO BILLS TAP HOMETOWN HEROES GOO GOO DOLLS FOR THANKSGIVING NIGHT HALFTIME CONCERT

Of course, the Bengals would prefer to host the AFC championship game themselves. They’re 7-2 heading into Monday Night Football against Washington, and I suspect they’ll be rooting for Kansas City on Thanksgiving. A Chiefs win would give Buffalo its second loss, and the Bengals don’t get a shot at the Bills in the regular season. They do, however, get the Chiefs at home on Dec. 13.

And yes, the Broncos and Jaguars are in the mix for the No. 1 seed, too. Jacksonville even went into Cincinnati and beat the Bengals. But when I ranked my Super Bowl contenders at the halfway point, I had three AFC teams in the top tier. If it’s my money, I’m still betting the AFC runs through Kansas City, Buffalo or Cincinnati.

So if the Chiefs win on Thanksgiving and the Bengals keep winning, Chiefs-Bengals on Dec. 13 might be the biggest game of the NFL regular season. That gives me about two weeks to ask my editor if changing "Bills" to "Bengals" and running this article again counts as plagiarizing myself.

Week 11 didn’t look particularly good on paper, and most of Sunday’s early games looked about the same on TV. If the NFL wants to wash the taste of those lopsided matchups out of our mouths, though, Week 12 ought to do it.

The Packers visit the Rams on Wednesday night. The Bears and Lions open Thanksgiving with a game that could help decide the NFC North, and we get Seahawks-49ers on Sunday afternoon. I’d happily watch any of those three, and none is the game I’m looking forward to most. That would be Chiefs-Bills on Thanksgiving night.

The only downside is that three of those four games will be over before we even get to Friday. Then again, am I really going to complain about only having to wait four days to see Mahomes and Allen play each other?

Ask me again Sunday at 1 p.m. when I’m trying to decide which game gets the main TV in my living room and Saints-Bengals is probably my best option.

item.title: Trump says Iran unleashed missile, drone surge after midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump says Iran launched more missiles and drones over the past week than at any point in over a year, and all were knocked down with no damage.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Sunday that Iran has launched more missiles and drones over the past week than at any point in more than a year, adding that U. S. forces shot them down without any damage and as tensions escalate following the U.S. midterm elections.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump also tied the surge in Iranian attacks to the Nov. 3 midterm elections, when Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress amid voter frustration over the war with Iran and rising fuel costs.

"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections," Trump wrote on Truth Social.

TRUMP RESPONDS AFTER VANCE BLAMES IRAN WAR FOR MIDTERM LOSSES, VP SAYS HIS JOB IS TO SUPPORT PRESIDENT

"One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran, which has killed 81,000 protestors as of today, will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred. "

Trump also said that Iran launched "more drones and missiles over the past week than at any time for over a year," though he said U.S. defenses neutralized the threat.

"Don't worry, they've all been knocked down, and done no damage," Trump said.

"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won't let that happen!" he added.

The remarks also came days after the Senate rejected a war powers resolution in a 48-51 vote on Nov. 19, leaving Trump's military authority intact.

TRUMP WARNS OF NEW STRIKES AGAINST IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR, CALLS NEGOTIATORS ‘PROFESSIONAL TAP DANCERS’

Speaking to Fox News earlier Sunday, Trump said he is inclined to resume strikes on Iran after the new year if diplomatic talks fail to produce a deal, warning that Iranian vessels testing the U.S. naval blockade would end up "at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy."

In his social media post Sunday, Trump accused both Democrats and Iran of trying to keep fuel prices high ahead of the midterm elections and separately questioned the integrity of the vote without providing evidence.

"Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," Trump wrote, adding that it was too bad voters "didn't understand this before they pulled the trigger."

"The whole Election was very 'strange,'" he said. "In the end, America will win! "

item.title: Travis Kelce passes Rob Gronkowski on all-time NFL list with two-touchdown game for Chiefs
item.description: Travis Kelce passed Rob Gronkowski for third on the NFL's all-time tight end touchdowns list, hauling in two scores as the Kansas City Chiefs rolled.
item.content:encoded:
Travis Kelce had himself a day against the Arizona Cardinals, and with two more touchdowns on his Pro Football Hall of Fame resume, he made some NFL history.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end’s eight-yard touchdown snag to get his team in the end zone first on Sunday at Arrowhead Stadium marked the 109th of his career.

Kelce moved past the great Rob Gronkowski for third on the NFL’s all-time tight end touchdowns list. They had been tied at 108 scores, which the New England Patriots star finished his career with.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Only Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115), both Hall of Fame tight ends, are above Kelce on the list. He certainly has a chance to live atop the list entirely one day if he continues to get opportunities like he did on Sunday.

Quarterback Patrick Mahomes found Kelce later in this 34-7 blowout at home for an even more impressive 22-yard touchdown grab, where the veteran pass-catcher fought off two tacklers before falling into the end zone.

Kelce, with his superstar wife Taylor Swift in her usual suite looking down on the field, hauled in six of his seven targets for 74 yards with his two scores.

Mahomes himself had a tremendous day when he dropped back, going 27-of-39 for 324 yards with three touchdowns. With the game very out of reach in the fourth quarter, key starters like Mahomes and Kelce were getting some rest on the sideline.

This Sunday also marked Kelce’s 100th regular season game at the beloved Arrowhead Stadium, making him only the fourth player in team history to do so. He’s spent his entire career in Kansas City, which took him in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft out of Cincinnati.

It’s unknown what the future holds for Kelce after this season, as retirement has been a topic of conversation in back-to-back offseasons. The question will likely pop up again after the 2026 campaign, though Kelce hasn’t given an indication of what he wishes to do just yet.

item.title: Ravens silenced Marlon Humphrey for his words but what they'll hear after another loss will pale in comparison
item.description: Ravens tried to address criticism with Humphrey suspension but cannot quiet noise after 35-33 to the Carolina Panthers, their sixth consecutive loss.
item.content:encoded:
Days after silencing Marlon Humphrey for his disparaging words about their city, the Baltimore Ravens are going to wish they could silence a significant portion of their fans.

Days after one of their coaches addressed the Humphrey issue, saying there is "freedom of speech but not freedom of consequences," the Ravens are staring at the consequences of being a bad football team.

Days after basically not accepting Humphrey's apology for what he said on his podcast, the Ravens owe Baltimore an apology for their play on the field.

RAVENS DIDN'T DISCIPLINE RECEIVER OVER DOMESTIC VIOLENCE ARREST BUT SUSPEND MARLON HUMPHREY OVER PODCAST COMMENTS

Carolina Panthers 35.

Baltimore Ravens 33.

Welcome to the week that was and the season it has been for the Ravens.

In a season that has been a bitter disappointment and now includes six consecutive losses, the Ravens spent two days last week addressing and re-addressing what seemed like an otherwise manageable controversy that Humphrey started.

WOMAN KILLED NEAR RAVENS STADIUM SAME DAY MARLON HUMPHREY SENT HOME FOR JOKE ABOUT BALTIMORE CRIMINALITY

Humphrey on his podcast was asked what it was Baltimore is best at making?

"They're best at making criminals," he replied half-jokingly.

The disparaging words lit a firestorm that became a national story last Wednesday and Thursday while the Ravens were trying to salvage this season. And it is unfortunate for everyone involved because ...

NFL RESTARTS SOCIAL JUSTICE MESSAGING WHILE BATTLING DOMESTIC ABUSE, DRUNK DRIVING AND PROSTITUTION ARRESTS

Let's handle that part first. Humphrey apologized immediately once this became a problem. And the Ravens seemed to accept that Wednesday as they prepared for Sunday's game against the Panthers.

But seeing the negative media attention and backlash from fans and politicians and on social media, the Ravens took an extra step by suspending Humphrey on Thursday.

The club in need of more talent, not less, sent one of its top four or five defensive backs home for the weekend and possibly longer.

The team could have as easily decided to make it clear that it believed Humphrey was wrong, he apologized, and it was onward to Carolina. But the club instead bowed to outside opinions.

All while making its secondary inside the team weaker.

Baltimore allowed 35 points against Carolina. No, that doesn't imply Baltimore would have been better on defense if Humphrey played. He's not the same player he was four or five years ago.

But the fact is his replacement Chidobe Awuzie gave up a touchdown pass.

And Baltimore allowed 35 points or more for only the third time this season while Carolina quarterback Bryce Young delivered his fourth-best passer rating of the season.

"At the end of the day we had a lead, we were on the field with a lead," coach Jesse Minter said. "We didn't hold it."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Humphrey's suspension surely changed the subject about this season for the Ravens for a couple of days last week. But the team that could not abide Humphrey's words better get used to much uglier things said about them in the coming days.

Some fringe (I think) Ravens fans spent time on social media both wondering about and calling for Minter to be fired after only one season. His agreement to suspend Humphrey didn't protect the coach from fans that care more about good results than good intentions.

Considering this was a team expected to compete for a postseason berth when the season began, this is now one of the club's most disappointing seasons in recent memory.

If Baltimore and the Ravens were offended by Humphrey's words, they surely should be hurting by that.

item.title: Trump dares Iran to breach US port blockade as Tehran reportedly readies 14 oil tankers
item.description: Iran reportedly positioned 14 tankers at Kharg Island to breach the U.S. blockade, as President Donald Trump dared Tehran to test American naval forces in the Gulf.
item.content:encoded:
Reports that Iran plans to send more than a dozen tankers through the U.S. blockade of its ports raised fears of a wider conflict Sunday, as a maritime security expert warned of a risky confrontation and President Donald Trump dared Tehran to test American forces deployed across the Gulf.

"I hope they do, they'll all be at the bottom of the sea like the rest of the navy," Trump told Fox News chief foreign correspondent Trey Yingst when asked whether Iran would attempt to breach the blockade, first imposed in April.

The warning came as reports indicated Iran was preparing a convoy of tankers to breach the blockade from Kharg Island, a critical oil export hub.

TRUMP DETAILS SWEEPING 'ALL OR NOTHING' BLOCKADE OF STRAIT OF HORMUZ AFTER FAILED IRAN TALKS

Maritime security experts warned the vessels could face U.S. naval forces right across the Indian Ocean, while the Institute for the Study of War cautioned that an attempted breakout could perhaps trigger a wider war.

The reported operation would involve tankers sailing from Kharg Island, which handles most of Iran's crude oil exports, toward the Gulf of Oman and with crews reportedly assigned to the vessels and Iranian flags raised ahead of a possible attempt to breach the blockade.

Charlie Brown, a senior adviser to United Against Nuclear Iran (UANI) and maritime sanctions enforcement expert, dismissed the reported operation as "propaganda" and said the plan was unlikely to succeed if ever attempted.

"This supposed plan by the Iranians to suddenly deploy 14 vessels to try to breach the blockade in a convoy — it's farcical," Brown told Fox News Digital on Sunday.

"The blockade is enforced not merely as a line that is crossed, but the ability of the United States Navy to enforce this blockade extends across the entire Indian Ocean and beyond."

BLOCKADE 101: AMERICAN SEA POWER ON DISPLAY AS TRUMP CORNERS IRAN AND WARNS OFF CHINA

"If ships try to get out of the area that is managed by the U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet, the U.S. Navy's 7th Fleet is the next area command that has responsibility over the Indian Ocean," he said.

"And they have ships and aircraft that are there right now, and they'll just take up the mission."

The potential confrontation comes amid rising maritime tensions. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported Sunday that a tanker was involved in an incident with military forces in the Gulf of Oman but did not identify the vessel or connect it to the reported Iranian convoy.

"UKMTO has received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman," the agency said in an advisory.

"Vessels are advised to consider the latest maritime security information and maintain awareness of the evolving operational environment."

The Institute for the Study of War (ISW) also warned Iran could attempt to break the blockade within days as mounting economic pressure leaves Tehran with few options.

"Iran's deteriorating economic situation is increasingly dire, which is forcing Iranian officials to reckon with the necessity of breaking the US blockade," the institute said in an update.

The assessment followed a Nov. 20 report by Hamshahri, a Tehran municipality-affiliated outlet, claiming Iran had positioned 14 tankers at Kharg Island to breach the blockade.

TRUMP BLOCKADE SQUEEZING IRAN SO HARD REGIME MAY BE DUMPING OIL INTO GULF, EXPERTS SAY

"Attempting to run the blockade would expose Iran to significant risk that ranges from the destruction of a tanker fleet at minimum to possibly resuming a larger-scale conflict with the United States, or both," the institute said.

"Iran's willingness to accept these risks demonstrates the degree to which the regime views the current economic situation as both dire and unsustainable."

Brown, however, questioned whether Tehran would send the tankers, suggesting the reported operation was an attempt to project defiance rather than a viable strategy.

"This supposed run of the blockade by several Iranian ships that's discussed is most likely propaganda — another one of a series of similar propaganda statements that don't turn out to be true and are easily debunked," he said.

Brown also disputed reports that the tankers were loaded and preparing to depart, citing satellite monitoring of Kharg Island.

"We carefully watched Kharg Island loading by satellite imagery, and there's really no indication that there's been any significant loading there in quite some time."

Brown said coordinating a 14-vessel convoy would also pose major logistical challenges, requiring lead and trailing ships, coordinated communications and procedures for responding to U.S. military orders.

Civilian crews could face significant danger if they refused orders to stop, he warned.

TRUMP WARNS OF NEW STRIKES AGAINST IRAN AFTER NEW YEAR, CALLS NEGOTIATORS ‘PROFESSIONAL TAP DANCERS’

"They would obviously be going into an area of great risk, and they would have to decide whether to comply with the instructions to stop or face action," Brown said.

In a Nov. 18 advisory, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) warned that ships receiving Iranian cargo through ship-to-ship transfers could face interception or seizure, extending the blockade beyond vessels departing Iranian ports, Reuters reported.

Brown said U.S. forces would likely contact the tankers by radio from Navy ships or aircraft and order them to stop. Refusal could trigger an escalated military response.

He said the Navy could transfer responsibility between regional commands, making it difficult for Iranian tankers to escape by sailing farther into the Indian Ocean.

"There's an administrative boundary, a geographic boundary between the 5th Fleet and the 7th Fleet, between CENTCOM and INDOPACOM," Brown said.

"But the U.S. Navy is a global Navy, and they're able to handle these transfers of responsibility when a target or ship of interest crosses that boundary."

Brown said U.S. forces have the ships, aircraft and procedures to intercept multiple vessels at once, while the open waters of the Indian Ocean offer more room to maneuver than the narrow Strait of Hormuz.

"It's a mission of the United States, not merely a mission in CENTCOM," Brown said. "So they have the forces in place."

"So if they do try to make an attempt with multiple ships, I'm quite confident all or most — probably all — would be interdicted," he added.

item.title: Mets, Tarik Skubal agree to record contract as MLB lockout looms over offseason
item.description: Tarik Skubal's record $450 million Mets deal features $30 million in deferrals and a $45 million signing bonus as MLB's Dec. 1 labor deadline looms.
item.content:encoded:
Two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal agreed to the richest pitching contract in baseball history Sunday.

New York agreed to terms with the ace on a nine-year, $450 million deal, according to multiple reports.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

At $50 million a year, the contract shatters Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s $325 million pitching record and clears the $43.33 million annual mark owned by Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander. Only Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. have bigger deals.

Baseball’s labor fight also drove an urgency to sign Skubal. With MLB's labor deal expiring Dec. 1, a lockout freezes signings amid a push for a salary cap.

Mets owner Steve Cohen outbid teams like the Dodgers, Toronto Blue Jays and San Diego Padres.

SOME OF MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL'S BIGGEST SUPERSTARS MIGHT BE ON THE MOVE BEFORE LOCKOUT STARTS

Los Angeles refused to match nine years given his three elbow surgeries. Skubal’s payday follows a 2026 season split between Detroit and Los Angeles.

After winning two Cy Youngs with the Tigers, he joined the Dodgers in a deadline trade, finishing with 12 wins, 186 strikeouts and a 2.72 ERA.

The contract features $30 million in deferrals and a $45 million signing bonus.

No opt-outs and a full no-trade clause mean Skubal is locked into Queens for the rest of his prime, whether a salary cap comes next or not.

After fighting through brutal seasons in Queens, the Mets are willing to show, at least through the checkbook, that they're all-in.
